preamble: Fronting of the open vowel /a/ to open-mid front /ɛ/. The textbook case is the Attic-Ionic shift of Proto-Greek long *ā to η [ɛː], which separates Attic and Ionic from Doric and Aeolic (Doric μάτηρ vs Attic μήτηρ 'mother'). In Ionic it happened in all positions; Attic kept ā after e, i and r. Gallo-Romance stressed a > e/ɛ (Latin mare > French mer) is usually reconstructed as passing through [æ], so it is not filed here.

examples.note: Proto-Greek long ā became η /ɛː/ in Attic-Ionic. Ionic made the change everywhere; Attic kept ā after e, i and r (Attic χώρα khṓrā vs Ionic χώρη khṓrē 'place, country').
